parts.text:
29 Observable interference fringes are produced using light from a double slit. The intensity of the
light emerging from each slit is initially the same.
The intensity of the light emerging from one of the slits is now reduced.
How does this affect the interference pattern?
A
The bright fringes and the dark fringes all become brighter.
B
The bright fringes and the dark fringes all become darker.
C
The bright fringes become brighter and the dark fringes become darker.
D
The bright fringes become darker and the dark fringes become brighter.

hints: Notice the starting condition: equal intensity from each slit gives fully dark minima and maximum contrast.
Recall that bright fringe amplitude is the sum $A_1 + A_2$ and dark fringe amplitude is the difference $|A_1 - A_2|$.
Ask what happens to the sum when one $A$ falls, and what happens to the difference when the two $A$ values are no longer equal.
walkthrough: Start with the two waves arriving from the slits with amplitudes $A_1$ and $A_2$. Initially $A_1 = A_2 = A$ because the slit intensities are equal.
At a bright fringe the waves meet in phase, so the resultant amplitude is $A_1 + A_2$. Initially this is $2A$, giving maximum intensity proportional to $(2A)^2$.
At a dark fringe the waves meet in antiphase, so the resultant amplitude is $|A_1 - A_2|$. Initially this is zero, giving a fully dark minimum.
Now reduce the intensity from one slit, so for example $A_2 < A_1$. The bright-fringe amplitude $A_1 + A_2$ is now less than $2A$, so the maximum intensity falls and bright fringes become darker.
The dark-fringe amplitude $|A_1 - A_2|$ is now greater than zero because cancellation is incomplete, so some intensity remains and dark fringes become brighter.
Reduced maxima with raised minima means lower fringe contrast. This is option D.

A.explanation: Reducing light from one slit cannot add energy to the pattern, so both sets of fringes cannot become brighter.

B.explanation: The bright fringes do become darker, but the dark fringes do not become darker because perfect cancellation is lost.

C.explanation: This describes increased contrast, whereas unequal slit amplitudes reduce the contrast between bright and dark fringes.

D.explanation: Less total light makes constructive overlap weaker, while incomplete cancellation makes destructive overlap less dark.
